LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To describe people’s appearance.
MATERIAL
•	 TR#16 Thief Song
•	 TR#17 Descriptions Song
•	 TR#20 Time to Go Home Song
•	 Calendar (P.E.M.1)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 10: face parts cutouts + 
Blu-Tack
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 6: Character cards (P.3.2)
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 7: Memory cards (P.3.7) + 
Character Bingo boards (P.3.7) 
•	 Teacher materials for Act. 8: Character (P.3.2) + Age 
cards (P.3.8)
•	 Pam&Paul Board Game
•	 Pam&Paul Board Game Reference Sheet
•	 Dice and Counters (1 per child)
BEFORE CLASS
If it’s the last day of the story, check the teacher’s dashboard

2.– ACTIVITY 10: DESCRIPTIONS SONG (TR#17) (3’)
> Main Activity
Stick up the individual blonde, black, long, short, curly and 
straight hair cutouts on the whiteboard or place them on the 
table before you play the track. For the eyes and mouth, you 
can just use gestures.

Every time you sing “Are you …?” hold up the palms of your 
hands in the air and then point in front of you when you say 
“You”. Then, perform the action as indicated in brackets below.
DESCRIPTIONS SONG
Are you young? 
(smile and imitate rocking a baby in your arms)
Are you old? 
(bend over and walk as if you are an elderly person with 
a walking stick)
Are you short? 
(put your hands down low)
Or are you tall? 
(put your hands up high)
Have you got big eyes?
(point to your eyes and make a big circle with your hands)
Or have you got small eyes?
(point to your eyes and make a small circle with your hands)
What do you look like? 
(point to anybody)
Tell me something more, I’d like to know! 
(point to yourself first and then hold up your hands 
indicating that you don’t know)
Have you got blonde hair? 
(point to the cutout)
Have you got black hair? 
(point to the cutout)
Is it long or short, curly or straight?  
(point to the cutouts) 
What do you look like? I think I know! 
(put your palms facing up then to your eyes and finish 
by pointing to your head)
3.– STORY QUESTIONS (8’)
There will not be any storytelling in today’s lesson, students 
will work on the story in a more fun way. The students will be 
asked questions about the story and will be expected to give 
the appropriate answers. You can bring along some props like 
a bandana or buzzer to make it even more fun.
Suggested questions are as follows:
•	 Where do Mum, Grandma, Grandpa, Pam and Paul go 
to have a picnic? They go to the park to have a picnic.
•	 What can’t Mum find? Mum can’t find her purse.
•	 What are they playing when Mum’s purse disappears? 
They are playing frisbee.
•	 Who saw the thief? Grandpa saw the thief.
•	 What does the thief look like? Is he tall or short? 
He is short.

•	 What colour are the thief’s eyes? He has got brown 
eyes.
•	 What colour hair has he got? He has got blonde hair. 
•	 Has he got straight hair or curly hair? He has got 
straight hair.
•	 Who stole Mum’s purse in the end? There was no 
thief. Billy has got Mum’s purse. It was a joke!
Please, note that these are only suggestions. You might want 
to expand them if you deem it necessary.

5.– ACTIVITY 6: INCORRECT DESCRIPTIONS (7’)
P.3.2
Joe
> How to Play
Choose a Character playing card (P.3.2) and show it to the 
Ss. Then incorrectly describe the person. Ss will have to correct 
you using full sentences.
> Warm-Up
To introduce the structures, start by saying wrong things 
about the Ss in the group. For example, if Jane has got blonde 
hair, say, “Jane has got brown hair. Is that right or wrong?”

Encourage Ss to correct you by saying, “No, that’s wrong. 
She hasn’t got brown hair. Jane has got blonde hair.”
Say two or three wrong statements about your Ss so they 
can practise correcting you.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Choose a Character playing card, show it to the Ss and make 
a mistake when describing the character. You can say, “Hmm, 
I think I’m a bit confused...” to make it more theatrical. The 
Ss must correct you by saying, for example, “No, that’s wrong. 
She hasn’t got blonde hair. She has got red hair.” Ss love to 
correct the teacher, so you can make this activity more fun by 
exaggerating your mistakes and acting surprised or confused 
when they correct you.
> For Advanced Groups
When your Ss get the gist of the activity, and they are familiar 
with the target language, you can let them take on the teacher 
role and incorrectly describe a character.
6.– ACTIVITY 7: CLOTHING DESCRIPTION MEMORY (8’)
P.3.7
P.3.7
P.3.7
P.3.7
> How to Play
Each flash card shows a character and a grid with three 
squares. Ss will have to find their character’s three body parts.
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the target language with a TPR activity. Start 
by saying, “If you are wearing a T-shirt, stand up!”. Repeat this 
at least three more times, changing the action they have to do. 
Then move on to review appearance. Say, “If you have got 
blue eyes, clap your hands.”. Repeat this step at least five more 
times, using expressions related to hair, eyes, mouth and nose.

NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Before class, group the Memory cards (P.3.7) based on the 
body part they show (head, body, legs and feet). Place the three 
groups of cards face down on the table. Give each S an A4 card 
and have them place it on the table in front of them. Introduce 
the activity by saying, “Let’s try to find the character on our 
board!”. The Ss must take it in turns to turn over one memory 
card from each group. They then need to identify if the cards 
they have turned match the character on their board. Use the 
following model to proceed:
•	 S: Turns over a “head” card, a “body” card, and a “legs 
and feet” card.
•	 T: “What does your character look like?”
•	 S: “He has got long blonde hair, but (pointing to the 
character on their card) he has got brown hair. It’s 
not a pair.”
•	 T: “What is your character wearing?”
•	 S: “He is wearing a blue jumper, and he is also wearing 
a blue jumper. It’s a pair! (The S places the card on 
their board). But (pointing to the body on their card) he 
is wearing green trousers and he isn’t. It’s not a pair!”. 
The game is over when you run out of time, or when a S 
completes their grid.
NOTE: if you have a large group, it is advisable to play this 
game in pairs. If you have a small group, you can have the S 
flip only one card per turn to make the activity more dynamic.	
> Follow-Up
When a S has finished the game or time has run out, you 
should a S to describe their character from head to toe by asking, 
“Tell me, what does your character look like?”
7.– ACTIVITY 8: HOW OLD ARE YOU? (6’)
P.3.2
Lisa
P.3.8
15
Lisa
> How to Play
Ss have to guess the age of a character by asking questions.

> Warm-Up
Ask your Ss, “How old are you?”, and encourage them to 
say, “I’m … years old.”. 
Next, pretend you’re confused and point to a S. Ask the group, 
“Is Jane 40 years old?”, to which they should answer, “No, she 
isn’t.”. Continue by asking, “Is she younger or older?” and let 
them answer, “She is younger.”. Finish by asking them about 
the correct age, “Is she 7?”, and encourage them to answer 
“Yes, she is!”.
Do one more example if needed.
NOTE: if your Ss are familiar with the target language, you 
may skip this step.
> Main Activity
Ss must guess the age of the different characters. Prepare 
two sets of cards, one with the character’s age (P.3.8) and one 
without (P.3.2). Choose a pair of cards of the same character, 
keep the age card in your hand and put the character card 
face up on the table for the Ss to see. Introduce the activity by 
saying, “Let’s see if you can guess how old the characters are!”.
If you take the Nancy card, for example, you can start by 
asking, “How old is Nancy?” and Ss must take it in turns asking, 
“Is she 20 years old?”, for example. You should then respond, 
“No, she isn’t.” and encourage Ss to ask, “Is she younger or 
older?” to which you should respond “She is older.”. When they 
are ready to guess the character’s age, they should ask, “Is she 
… years old?”. Once the Ss have guessed correctly, show the 
card with the age of the character and let one of the Ss have 
a turn at choosing a card.
> Follow-Up
Show the character cards without the age and ask, “Do you 
remember how old Michelle is?” to which Ss should answer, 
“Michelle is thirty-three years old.”. Try to let each S participate 
at least once.
8.– PAM&PAUL BOARD GAME (15’)
P.E.M.4.1
START
FINISH
P.E.M.4

Play as many rounds of the Pam&Paul Board Game as time 
allows.
SET-UP
1.	 The game can be played individually or in groups (this is 
recommended for big groups). Each player/pair chooses 
a counter and places it on the start square.
2.	 Start the game using one of the strategies in the “Starting 
a game” section in the introduction of the TG. 
3.	 Have them roll the dice and move their counter. Depending 
on the colour of the square (category) the Ss land on, ask 
them to perform the challenge mentioned in the Board 
Game Reference Sheet. 
Special squares:
•	 Square with a plane on it: follow the dotted line and 
go back to the start.
•	 Square with Billy on it: follow Billy’s footprints and 
do the challenge.
•	 Square with a bicycle on it: ride down the road and 
do the challenge.
4.	 If they perform the challenge correctly, they can stay 
on the square. If not, give them a second chance by 
rewording or giving them clues. If they still can’t get it, 
they go back to the square they were in before.
5.	 The game ends when someone reaches the finish line.
9.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’) 
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line 
before leaving the class. 
BONUS
ACTIVITY 2: GUESS WHO
P.3.2
Joe
> Main Activity
This activity is based on the popular board game Guess Who.

Model this activity for the Ss the first time you do it. Introduce 
it by saying, “Let’s see if you can guess the character!”. Place 
the A5 cards (P.3.2) on the table to use as a reference. Shuffle 
the individual playing cards (P.3.2) and let a S choose a card 
without letting the rest of the group see it. The group should 
take it in turns to ask their classmate different questions to try 
to guess who they are such as, “Jane, have you got red hair?”, 
to which they should respond either “Yes, I have,” or “No, I 
haven’t.” If they say, “No, I haven’t,” the group must turn over 
the A5 card with characters that have red hair to rule them out.
Ss may also ask if the character is a boy or a girl, young or 
old and the clothing items they are wearing. Let Ss continue in 
this manner until they guess who the character is. When one 
of the Ss thinks that they know who their classmate is, they 
should ask, “Are you…?” and the other S must respond, “Yes, 
I am/No, I’m not.”. Each S can only make one guess, and they 
have to skip a turn if they get it wrong (this ensures they don’t 
go straight to asking who the character is).
ACTIVITY 11: NUMBERS (VERSION 3)
P.E.M.3
55
This is a relay game. Divide the class into two teams. Get 
each team to form a line in front of the whiteboard. Give each 
team a whiteboard marker, draw a card from the deck (P.E.M.3.) 
and call out the number. One S from each team must run to 
the board and write the number. Say as many numbers as 
time allows. Then check these numbers using the cards. The 
team with the most correct numbers written on the board wins.
NOTE: it might be helpful to divide the board into two (Team 1, 
Team 2) and to make each team line up in front of their section.
